findings.summary: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the following `setInterval(...)` call never assigns its return value to it (should be `pingTimer=setInterval(...)`). `ws.onclose` then calls `clearInterval(pingTimer)` on `undefined`, which is a no-op. Every call to connect() — the initial one and every reconnect after a drop — starts a brand-new interval that is never cleared, so repeated reconnects (e.g. a flaky network) leave multiple ping loops running concurrently, each sending 'ping' every 15s. This is exactly the failure mode the brief explicitly asked to be prevented: 'make sure the ping timer from a previous connection is torn down when the socket closes, so reconnecting doesn't leave multiple ping loops running concurrently.'

findings.summary: The new test only checks for the literal substrings `setInterval(function(){`, `ws.send('ping')`, and `clearInterval(pingTimer)` in the emitted script text; it never executes the script against a mock WebSocket, so it can't detect that the interval id is never actually captured/cleared. This matches the file's existing convention of asserting on generated script text rather than executing it (other tests in the same describe block do the same), so it isn't 'gaming' relative to its peers — but it means the Critical bug above passes the suite undetected.
